issues.legal_issue: A provincial legislature lacks competence to enact a law for the compulsory acquisition of a commercial or industrial undertaking when no legislative entry authorizes that acquisition and no special authorization has been granted.
material_facts: The challenged legislation provided for the compulsory acquisition of electricity-supply undertakings; its substance was acquisition, not the regulation or licensing of electricity supply or the regulation of corporations.
The government made an order declaring that the undertaking of an electricity-supply company would vest in it under the legislation.
The legislative lists contained no entry authorizing compulsory acquisition of a commercial or industrial undertaking, and no special authorization to enact the legislation had been issued.
The company challenged the acquisition order by writ, and the appeal followed the rejection of that challenge.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed because the provincial legislature lacked legislative competence to enact the acquisition law.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 99 and 100 of the Government of India Act, 1935 distributed legislative powers according to the entries in the Seventh Schedule. Section 299(2) contemplated laws authorizing compulsory acquisition of commercial or industrial undertakings but did not itself confer legislative competence. Entry 9 of List II authorized provincial legislation for compulsory acquisition of land only; section 104 provided for special authorization to legislate on an unenumerated matter. The broad incidental or ancillary powers associated with legislative entries did not supply a power to acquire such undertakings, a conclusion supported by section 127 and the reasoning in State of Bihar v. Maharajadhiraja Sir Kameshwar Singh, [1952] S.C.R. 889.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_challenge and provincial_legislature_enacted_acquisition_law and law_targets_compulsory_acquisition_of_commercial_undertaking and acquisition_power_absent_from_lists and not special_authorization_granted

predicates.appeal_from_writ_challenge: A party appealed after a court rejected its writ challenge to an acquisition order.
predicates.provincial_legislature_enacted_acquisiti: A provincial legislature enacted the law under which the acquisition was made.
predicates.law_targets_compulsory_acquisition_of_co: The law's substance was to provide for compulsory acquisition of a commercial or industrial undertaking.
predicates.acquisition_power_absent_from_lists: The applicable legislative lists contained no entry assigning the power to legislate for compulsory acquisition of such an undertaking.
predicates.special_authorization_granted: A special authorization was issued empowering the legislature to legislate on the otherwise unassigned matter.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a writ challenge concerns a provincial legislature's law for compulsory acquisition of a commercial or industrial undertaking, and the lists assign no such power and no special authorization was granted, the law is beyond legislative competence.
